modules.desc:
Type: Runtime

Users of MakeCallback that add the domain property to carry context, should start using the async_context variant of MakeCallback or CallbackScope, or the high-level AsyncResource class.

modules.name: dep0098:_asynchooks_embedder_`asyncresource.emitbefore`_and_`asyncresource.emitafter`_apis

changes.description: End-of-Life.
Runtime deprecation.

modules.desc:
Type: End-of-Life

The embedded API provided by AsyncHooks exposes .emitBefore() and .emitAfter() methods which are very easy to use incorrectly which can lead to unrecoverable errors.

Use asyncResource.runInAsyncScope() API instead which provides a much safer, and more convenient, alternative. See https://github.com/nodejs/node/pull/18513.

modules.name: dep0099:_async_context-unaware_`node::makecallback`_c++_apis

changes.description: Compile-time deprecation.

modules.desc:
Type: Compile-time

Certain versions of node::MakeCallback APIs available to native addons are deprecated. Please use the versions of the API that accept an async_context parameter.

modules.name: dep0100:_`process.assert()`

changes.description: Runtime deprecation.
Documentation-only deprecation.

modules.desc:
Type: Runtime

process.assert() is deprecated. Please use the assert module instead.

This was never a documented feature.

modules.name: dep0101:_`--with-lttng`

changes.description: End-of-Life.

modules.desc:
Type: End-of-Life

The --with-lttng compile-time option has been removed.

modules.name: dep0102:_using_`noassert`_in_`buffer#(read|write)`_operations

changes.description: End-of-Life.

modules.desc:
Type: End-of-Life

Using the noAssert argument has no functionality anymore. All input is verified regardless of the value of noAssert. Skipping the verification could lead to hard-to-find errors and crashes.

modules.name: dep0103:_`process.binding('util').is[...]`_typechecks

changes.description: Superseded by [DEP0111](#DEP0111).
Documentation-only deprecation.

modules.desc:
Type: Documentation-only (supports --pending-deprecation)

Using process.binding() in general should be avoided. The type checking methods in particular can be replaced by using util.types.

This deprecation has been superseded by the deprecation of the process.binding() API (DEP0111).

modules.name: dep0104:_`process.env`_string_coercion

changes.description: Documentation-only deprecation.

modules.desc:
Type: Documentation-only (supports --pending-deprecation)

When assigning a non-string property to process.env, the assigned value is implicitly converted to a string. This behavior is deprecated if the assigned value is not a string, boolean, or number. In the future, such assignment might result in a thrown error. Please convert the property to a string before assigning it to process.env.

modules.name: dep0105:_`decipher.finaltol`

changes.description: End-of-Life.
Runtime deprecation.

modules.desc:
Type: End-of-Life

decipher.finaltol() has never been documented and was an alias for decipher.final(). This API has been removed, and it is recommended to use decipher.final() instead.

modules.name: dep0106:_`crypto.createcipher`_and_`crypto.createdecipher`

changes.description: Runtime deprecation.
Documentation-only deprecation.

modules.desc:
Type: Runtime

Using crypto.createCipher() and crypto.createDecipher() must be avoided as they use a weak key derivation function (MD5 with no salt) and static initialization vectors. It is recommended to derive a key using crypto.pbkdf2() or crypto.scrypt() with random salts and to use crypto.createCipheriv() and crypto.createDecipheriv() to obtain the Cipher and Decipher objects respectively.

modules.name: dep0107:_`tls.convertnpnprotocols()`

changes.description: End-of-Life.
Runtime deprecation.

modules.desc:
Type: End-of-Life

This was an undocumented helper function not intended for use outside Node.js core and obsoleted by the removal of NPN (Next Protocol Negotiation) support.

modules.name: dep0108:_`zlib.bytesread`

changes.description: Runtime deprecation.
Documentation-only deprecation.

modules.desc:
Type: Runtime

Deprecated alias for zlib.bytesWritten. This original name was chosen because it also made sense to interpret the value as the number of bytes read by the engine, but is inconsistent with other streams in Node.js that expose values under these names.

modules.textRaw: DEP0109: `http`, `https`, and `tls` support for invalid URLs
modules.name: dep0109:_`http`,_`https`,_and_`tls`_support_for_invalid_urls

changes.description: End-of-Life.
Runtime deprecation.

modules.desc:
Type: End-of-Life

Some previously supported (but strictly invalid) URLs were accepted through the http.request(), http.get(), https.request(), https.get(), and tls.checkServerIdentity() APIs because those were accepted by the legacy url.parse() API. The mentioned APIs now use the WHATWG URL parser that requires strictly valid URLs. Passing an invalid URL is deprecated and support will be removed in the future.
modules.displayName: DEP0109: `http`, `https`, and `tls` support for invalid URLs

modules.name: dep0110:_`vm.script`_cached_data

changes.description: Documentation-only deprecation.

modules.desc:
Type: Documentation-only

The produceCachedData option is deprecated. Use script.createCachedData() instead.

modules.name: dep0111:_`process.binding()`

changes.description: Added support for `--pending-deprecation`.
Documentation-only deprecation.

modules.desc:
Type: Documentation-only (supports --pending-deprecation)

process.binding() is for use by Node.js internal code only.

While process.binding() has not reached End-of-Life status in general, it is unavailable when policies or the permission model are enabled.

modules.name: dep0112:_`dgram`_private_apis

changes.description: Runtime deprecation.

modules.desc:
Type: Runtime

The node:dgram module previously contained several APIs that were never meant to accessed outside of Node.js core: Socket.prototype._handle, Socket.prototype._receiving, Socket.prototype._bindState, Socket.prototype._queue, Socket.prototype._reuseAddr, Socket.prototype._healthCheck(), Socket.prototype._stopReceiving(), and dgram._createSocketHandle().

modules.name: dep0113:_`cipher.setauthtag()`,_`decipher.getauthtag()`

changes.description: End-of-Life.
Runtime deprecation.

modules.desc:
Type: End-of-Life

Cipher.setAuthTag() and Decipher.getAuthTag() are no longer available. They were never documented and would throw when called.

modules.name: dep0114:_`crypto._tobuf()`

changes.description: End-of-Life.
Runtime deprecation.

modules.desc:
Type: End-of-Life

The crypto._toBuf() function was not designed to be used by modules outside of Node.js core and was removed.

modules.name: dep0115:_`crypto.prng()`,_`crypto.pseudorandombytes()`,_`crypto.rng()`

changes.description: Added documentation-only deprecation with `--pending-deprecation` support.

modules.desc:
Type: Documentation-only (supports --pending-deprecation)

In recent versions of Node.js, there is no difference between crypto.randomBytes() and crypto.pseudoRandomBytes(). The latter is deprecated along with the undocumented aliases crypto.prng() and crypto.rng() in favor of crypto.randomBytes() and might be removed in a future release.

modules.name: dep0116:_legacy_url_api

changes.description: \`url.parse()` is deprecated again in DEP0169.
Deprecation revoked. Status changed to "Legacy".
Documentation-only deprecation.

modules.desc:
Type: Deprecation revoked

The legacy URL API is deprecated. This includes url.format(), url.parse(), url.resolve(), and the legacy urlObject. Please use the WHATWG URL API instead.

modules.name: dep0117:_native_crypto_handles

changes.description: End-of-Life.
Runtime deprecation.

modules.desc:
Type: End-of-Life

Previous versions of Node.js exposed handles to internal native objects through the _handle property of the Cipher, Decipher, DiffieHellman, DiffieHellmanGroup, ECDH, Hash, Hmac, Sign, and Verify classes. The _handle property has been removed because improper use of the native object can lead to crashing the application.

modules.textRaw: DEP0118: `dns.lookup()` support for a falsy host name
modules.name: dep0118:_`dns.lookup()`_support_for_a_falsy_host_name

changes.description: Runtime deprecation.

modules.desc:
Type: Runtime

Previous versions of Node.js supported dns.lookup() with a falsy host name like dns.lookup(false) due to backward compatibility. This behavior is undocumented and is thought to be unused in real world apps. It will become an error in future versions of Node.js.
modules.displayName: DEP0118: `dns.lookup()` support for a falsy host name

modules.name: dep0119:_`process.binding('uv').errname()`_private_api

changes.description: Documentation-only deprecation.

modules.desc:
Type: Documentation-only (supports --pending-deprecation)

process.binding('uv').errname() is deprecated. Please use util.getSystemErrorName() instead.

modules.name: dep0120:_windows_performance_counter_support

changes.description: End-of-Life.
Runtime deprecation.

modules.desc:
Type: End-of-Life

Windows Performance Counter support has been removed from Node.js. The undocumented COUNTER_NET_SERVER_CONNECTION(), COUNTER_NET_SERVER_CONNECTION_CLOSE(), COUNTER_HTTP_SERVER_REQUEST(), COUNTER_HTTP_SERVER_RESPONSE(), COUNTER_HTTP_CLIENT_REQUEST(), and COUNTER_HTTP_CLIENT_RESPONSE() functions have been deprecated.

modules.name: dep0121:_`net._setsimultaneousaccepts()`

changes.description: Runtime deprecation.

modules.desc:
Type: Runtime

The undocumented net._setSimultaneousAccepts() function was originally intended for debugging and performance tuning when using the node:child_process and node:cluster modules on Windows. The function is not generally useful and is being removed. See discussion here: https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/18391

modules.name: dep0122:_`tls`_`server.prototype.setoptions()`

changes.description: Runtime deprecation.

modules.desc:
Type: Runtime

Please use Server.prototype.setSecureContext() instead.

modules.textRaw: DEP0123: setting the TLS ServerName to an IP address
modules.name: dep0123:_setting_the_tls_servername_to_an_ip_address

changes.description: Runtime deprecation.

modules.desc:
Type: Runtime

Setting the TLS ServerName to an IP address is not permitted by RFC 6066. This will be ignored in a future version.
modules.displayName: DEP0123: setting the TLS ServerName to an IP address

modules.name: dep0124:_using_`replserver.rli`

changes.description: End-of-Life.
Runtime deprecation.

modules.desc:
Type: End-of-Life

This property is a reference to the instance itself.

modules.name: dep0125:_`require('node:_stream_wrap')`

changes.description: Runtime deprecation.

modules.desc:
Type: Runtime

The node:_stream_wrap module is deprecated.

modules.name: dep0126:_`timers.active()`

changes.description: Runtime deprecation.

modules.desc:
Type: Runtime

The previously undocumented timers.active() is deprecated. Please use the publicly documented timeout.refresh() instead. If re-referencing the timeout is necessary, timeout.ref() can be used with no performance impact since Node.js 10.

modules.name: dep0127:_`timers._unrefactive()`

changes.description: Runtime deprecation.

modules.desc:
Type: Runtime

The previously undocumented and "private" timers._unrefActive() is deprecated. Please use the publicly documented timeout.refresh() instead. If unreferencing the timeout is necessary, timeout.unref() can be used with no performance impact since Node.js 10.

modules.textRaw: DEP0128: modules with an invalid `main` entry and an `index.js` file
modules.name: dep0128:_modules_with_an_invalid_`main`_entry_and_an_`index.js`_file

changes.description: Runtime deprecation.
Documentation-only.

modules.desc:
Type: Runtime

Modules that have an invalid main entry (e.g., ./does-not-exist.js) and also have an index.js file in the top level directory will resolve the index.js file. That is deprecated and is going to throw an error in future Node.js versions.
modules.displayName: DEP0128: modules with an invalid `main` entry and an `index.js` file

modules.name: dep0129:_`childprocess._channel`

changes.description: Runtime deprecation.
Documentation-only.

modules.desc:
Type: Runtime

The _channel property of child process objects returned by spawn() and similar functions is not intended for public use. Use ChildProcess.channel instead.

modules.name: dep0130:_`module.createrequirefrompath()`

changes.description: End-of-life.
Runtime deprecation.
Documentation-only.

modules.desc:
Type: End-of-Life

Use module.createRequire() instead.

modules.name: dep0131:_legacy_http_parser

changes.description: This feature has been removed.
Runtime deprecation.
Documentation-only.

modules.desc:
Type: End-of-Life

The legacy HTTP parser, used by default in versions of Node.js prior to 12.0.0, is deprecated and has been removed in v13.0.0. Prior to v13.0.0, the --http-parser=legacy command-line flag could be used to revert to using the legacy parser.

modules.name: dep0132:_`worker.terminate()`_with_callback

changes.description: Runtime deprecation.

modules.desc:
Type: Runtime

Passing a callback to worker.terminate() is deprecated. Use the returned Promise instead, or a listener to the worker's 'exit' event.

modules.name: dep0133:_`http`_`connection`

changes.description: Documentation-only deprecation.

modules.desc:
Type: Documentation-only

Prefer response.socket over response.connection and request.socket over request.connection.

modules.name: dep0134:_`process._tickcallback`

changes.description: Documentation-only deprecation.

modules.desc:
Type: Documentation-only (supports --pending-deprecation)

The process._tickCallback property was never documented as an officially supported API.

modules.name: dep0135:_`writestream.open()`_and_`readstream.open()`_are_internal

changes.description: Runtime deprecation.

modules.desc:
Type: Runtime

WriteStream.open() and ReadStream.open() are undocumented internal APIs that do not make sense to use in userland. File streams should always be opened through their corresponding factory methods fs.createWriteStream() and fs.createReadStream()) or by passing a file descriptor in options.

modules.name: dep0136:_`http`_`finished`

changes.description: Documentation-only deprecation.

modules.desc:
Type: Documentation-only

response.finished indicates whether response.end() has been called, not whether 'finish' has been emitted and the underlying data is flushed.

Use response.writableFinished or response.writableEnded accordingly instead to avoid the ambiguity.

To maintain existing behavior response.finished should be replaced with response.writableEnded.

modules.textRaw: DEP0137: Closing fs.FileHandle on garbage collection
modules.name: dep0137:_closing_fs.filehandle_on_garbage_collection

changes.description: Runtime deprecation.

modules.desc:
Type: Runtime

Allowing a fs.FileHandle object to be closed on garbage collection is deprecated. In the future, doing so might result in a thrown error that will terminate the process.

Please ensure that all fs.FileHandle objects are explicitly closed using FileHandle.prototype.close() when the fs.FileHandle is no longer needed:

const fsPromises = require('node:fs').promises;
async function openAndClose() {
  let filehandle;
  try {
    filehandle = await fsPromises.open('thefile.txt', 'r');
  } finally {
    if (filehandle !== undefined)
      await filehandle.close();
  }
}
modules.displayName: DEP0137: Closing fs.FileHandle on garbage collection

modules.name: dep0138:_`process.mainmodule`

changes.description: Documentation-only deprecation.

modules.desc:
Type: Documentation-only

process.mainModule is a CommonJS-only feature while process global object is shared with non-CommonJS environment. Its use within ECMAScript modules is unsupported.

It is deprecated in favor of require.main, because it serves the same purpose and is only available on CommonJS environment.

modules.name: dep0139:_`process.umask()`_with_no_arguments

changes.description: Documentation-only deprecation.

modules.desc:
Type: Documentation-only

Calling process.umask() with no argument causes the process-wide umask to be written twice. This introduces a race condition between threads, and is a potential security vulnerability. There is no safe, cross-platform alternative API.

modules.name: dep0140:_use_`request.destroy()`_instead_of_`request.abort()`

changes.description: Documentation-only deprecation.

modules.desc:
Type: Documentation-only

Use request.destroy() instead of request.abort().

modules.name: dep0141:_`repl.inputstream`_and_`repl.outputstream`

changes.description: Documentation-only (supports [`--pending-deprecation`][]).

modules.desc:
Type: Documentation-only (supports --pending-deprecation)

The node:repl module exported the input and output stream twice. Use .input instead of .inputStream and .output instead of .outputStream.

modules.name: dep0142:_`repl._builtinlibs`

changes.description: Documentation-only (supports [`--pending-deprecation`][]).

modules.desc:
Type: Documentation-only

The node:repl module exports a _builtinLibs property that contains an array of built-in modules. It was incomplete so far and instead it's better to rely upon require('node:module').builtinModules.

modules.name: dep0143:_`transform._transformstate`

changes.description: Runtime deprecation.

modules.desc: Type: Runtime Transform._transformState will be removed in future versions where it is no longer required due to simplification of the implementation.

modules.name: dep0144:_`module.parent`

changes.description: Documentation-only deprecation.

modules.desc:
Type: Documentation-only (supports --pending-deprecation)

A CommonJS module can access the first module that required it using module.parent. This feature is deprecated because it does not work consistently in the presence of ECMAScript modules and because it gives an inaccurate representation of the CommonJS module graph.

Some modules use it to check if they are the entry point of the current process. Instead, it is recommended to compare require.main and module:

if (require.main === module) {
  // Code section that will run only if current file is the entry point.
}

When looking for the CommonJS modules that have required the current one, require.cache and module.children can be used:

const moduleParents = Object.values(require.cache)
  .filter((m) => m.children.includes(module));

modules.name: dep0145:_`socket.buffersize`

changes.description: Documentation-only deprecation.

modules.desc:
Type: Documentation-only

socket.bufferSize is just an alias for writable.writableLength.

modules.name: dep0146:_`new_crypto.certificate()`

changes.description: Documentation-only deprecation.

modules.desc:
Type: Documentation-only

The crypto.Certificate() constructor is deprecated. Use static methods of crypto.Certificate() instead.

modules.name: dep0147:_`fs.rmdir(path,_{_recursive:_true_})`

changes.description: Runtime deprecation.
Runtime deprecation for permissive behavior.
Documentation-only deprecation.

modules.desc:
Type: Runtime

In future versions of Node.js, recursive option will be ignored for fs.rmdir, fs.rmdirSync, and fs.promises.rmdir.

Use fs.rm(path, { recursive: true, force: true }), fs.rmSync(path, { recursive: true, force: true }) or fs.promises.rm(path, { recursive: true, force: true }) instead.

modules.name: dep0148:_folder_mappings_in_`"exports"`_(trailing_`"/"`)

changes.description: End-of-Life.
Runtime deprecation.
Runtime deprecation for self-referencing imports.
Documentation-only deprecation.

modules.desc:
Type: Runtime

Using a trailing "/" to define subpath folder mappings in the subpath exports or subpath imports fields is deprecated. Use subpath patterns instead.

modules.name: dep0149:_`http.incomingmessage#connection`

changes.description: Documentation-only deprecation.

modules.desc:
Type: Documentation-only.

Prefer message.socket over message.connection.

modules.name: dep0150:_changing_the_value_of_`process.config`

changes.description: End-of-Life.
Runtime deprecation.

modules.desc:
Type: End-of-Life

The process.config property provides access to Node.js compile-time settings. However, the property is mutable and therefore subject to tampering. The ability to change the value will be removed in a future version of Node.js.

modules.textRaw: DEP0151: Main index lookup and extension searching
modules.name: dep0151:_main_index_lookup_and_extension_searching

changes.description: Runtime deprecation.
Documentation-only deprecation with `--pending-deprecation` support.

modules.desc:
Type: Runtime

Previously, index.js and extension searching lookups would apply to import 'pkg' main entry point resolution, even when resolving ES modules.

With this deprecation, all ES module main entry point resolutions require an explicit "exports" or "main" entry with the exact file extension.
modules.displayName: DEP0151: Main index lookup and extension searching

modules.name: dep0152:_extension_performanceentry_properties

changes.description: Runtime deprecation.

modules.desc:
Type: Runtime

The 'gc', 'http2', and 'http' <PerformanceEntry> object types have additional properties assigned to them that provide additional information. These properties are now available within the standard detail property of the PerformanceEntry object. The existing accessors have been deprecated and should no longer be used.

modules.name: dep0153:_`dns.lookup`_and_`dnspromises.lookup`_options_type_coercion

changes.description: End-of-Life.
Runtime deprecation.
Documentation-only deprecation.

modules.desc:
Type: End-of-Life

Using a non-nullish non-integer value for family option, a non-nullish non-number value for hints option, a non-nullish non-boolean value for all option, or a non-nullish non-boolean value for verbatim option in dns.lookup() and dnsPromises.lookup() throws an ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE error.

modules.textRaw: DEP0154: RSA-PSS generate key pair options
modules.name: dep0154:_rsa-pss_generate_key_pair_options

changes.description: Runtime deprecation.
Documentation-only deprecation.

modules.desc:
Type: Runtime

The 'hash' and 'mgf1Hash' options are replaced with 'hashAlgorithm' and 'mgf1HashAlgorithm'.
modules.displayName: DEP0154: RSA-PSS generate key pair options

modules.textRaw: DEP0155: Trailing slashes in pattern specifier resolutions
modules.name: dep0155:_trailing_slashes_in_pattern_specifier_resolutions

changes.description: Runtime deprecation.
Documentation-only deprecation with `--pending-deprecation` support.

modules.desc:
Type: Runtime

The remapping of specifiers ending in "/" like import 'pkg/x/' is deprecated for package "exports" and "imports" pattern resolutions.
modules.displayName: DEP0155: Trailing slashes in pattern specifier resolutions

modules.name: dep0156:_`.aborted`_property_and_`'abort'`,_`'aborted'`_event_in_`http`

changes.description: Documentation-only deprecation.

modules.desc:
Type: Documentation-only

Move to <Stream> API instead, as the http.ClientRequest, http.ServerResponse, and http.IncomingMessage are all stream-based. Check stream.destroyed instead of the .aborted property, and listen for 'close' instead of 'abort', 'aborted' event.

The .aborted property and 'abort' event are only useful for detecting .abort() calls. For closing a request early, use the Stream .destroy([error]) then check the .destroyed property and 'close' event should have the same effect. The receiving end should also check the readable.readableEnded value on http.IncomingMessage to get whether it was an aborted or graceful destroy.

modules.name: dep0157:_thenable_support_in_streams

changes.description: End-of-life.
Documentation-only deprecation.

modules.desc:
Type: End-of-Life

An undocumented feature of Node.js streams was to support thenables in implementation methods. This is now deprecated, use callbacks instead and avoid use of async function for streams implementation methods.

This feature caused users to encounter unexpected problems where the user implements the function in callback style but uses e.g. an async method which would cause an error since mixing promise and callback semantics is not valid.

const w = new Writable({
  async final(callback) {
    await someOp();
    callback();
  },
});

modules.name: dep0158:_`buffer.slice(start,_end)`

changes.description: Documentation-only deprecation.

modules.desc:
Type: Documentation-only

This method was deprecated because it is not compatible with Uint8Array.prototype.slice(), which is a superclass of Buffer.

Use buffer.subarray which does the same thing instead.

modules.name: dep0159:_`err_invalid_callback`

changes.description: End-of-Life.

modules.desc:
Type: End-of-Life

This error code was removed due to adding more confusion to the errors used for value type validation.

modules.name: dep0160:_`process.on('multipleresolves',_handler)`

changes.description: Runtime deprecation.
Documentation-only deprecation.

modules.desc:
Type: Runtime.

This event was deprecated because it did not work with V8 promise combinators which diminished its usefulness.

modules.name: dep0161:_`process._getactiverequests()`_and_`process._getactivehandles()`

changes.description: Documentation-only deprecation.

modules.desc:
Type: Documentation-only

The process._getActiveHandles() and process._getActiveRequests() functions are not intended for public use and can be removed in future releases.

Use process.getActiveResourcesInfo() to get a list of types of active resources and not the actual references.

modules.name: dep0162:_`fs.write()`,_`fs.writefilesync()`_coercion_to_string

changes.description: End-of-Life.
Runtime deprecation.
Documentation-only deprecation.

modules.desc:
Type: End-of-Life

Implicit coercion of objects with own toString property, passed as second parameter in fs.write(), fs.writeFile(), fs.appendFile(), fs.writeFileSync(), and fs.appendFileSync() is deprecated. Convert them to primitive strings.

modules.name: dep0163:_`channel.subscribe(onmessage)`,_`channel.unsubscribe(onmessage)`

changes.description: Documentation-only deprecation.

modules.desc:
Type: Documentation-only

These methods were deprecated because they can be used in a way which does not hold the channel reference alive long enough to receive the events.

Use diagnostics_channel.subscribe(name, onMessage) or diagnostics_channel.unsubscribe(name, onMessage) which does the same thing instead.

modules.name: dep0164:_`process.exit(code)`,_`process.exitcode`_coercion_to_integer

changes.description: End-of-Life.
Runtime deprecation.
Documentation-only deprecation of `process.exitCode` integer coercion.
Documentation-only deprecation of `process.exit(code)` integer coercion.

modules.desc:
Type: End-of-Life

Values other than undefined, null, integer numbers, and integer strings (e.g., '1') are deprecated as value for the code parameter in process.exit() and as value to assign to process.exitCode.

modules.name: dep0165:_`--trace-atomics-wait`

changes.description: Documentation-only deprecation.

modules.desc:
Type: Documentation-only

The --trace-atomics-wait flag is deprecated.

modules.textRaw: DEP0166: Double slashes in imports and exports targets
modules.name: dep0166:_double_slashes_in_imports_and_exports_targets

changes.description: Runtime deprecation.
Documentation-only deprecation with `--pending-deprecation` support.

modules.desc:
Type: Runtime

Package imports and exports targets mapping into paths including a double slash (of "/" or "\") are deprecated and will fail with a resolution validation error in a future release. This same deprecation also applies to pattern matches starting or ending in a slash.
modules.displayName: DEP0166: Double slashes in imports and exports targets

modules.name: dep0167:_weak_`diffiehellmangroup`_instances_(`modp1`,_`modp2`,_`modp5`)

changes.description: Documentation-only deprecation.

modules.desc:
Type: Documentation-only

The well-known MODP groups modp1, modp2, and modp5 are deprecated because they are not secure against practical attacks. See RFC 8247 Section 2.4 for details.

These groups might be removed in future versions of Node.js. Applications that rely on these groups should evaluate using stronger MODP groups instead.

modules.textRaw: DEP0168: Unhandled exception in Node-API callbacks
modules.name: dep0168:_unhandled_exception_in_node-api_callbacks

changes.description: Runtime deprecation.

modules.desc:
Type: Runtime

The implicit suppression of uncaught exceptions in Node-API callbacks is now deprecated.

Set the flag --force-node-api-uncaught-exceptions-policy to force Node.js to emit an 'uncaughtException' event if the exception is not handled in Node-API callbacks.
modules.displayName: DEP0168: Unhandled exception in Node-API callbacks

modules.name: dep0169:_insecure_url.parse()

changes.description: Added support for `--pending-deprecation`.
Documentation-only deprecation.

modules.desc:
Type: Documentation-only (supports --pending-deprecation)

url.parse() behavior is not standardized and prone to errors that have security implications. Use the WHATWG URL API instead. CVEs are not issued for url.parse() vulnerabilities.

modules.name: dep0170:_invalid_port_when_using_`url.parse()`

changes.description: Runtime deprecation.

modules.textRaw: DEP0182: Short GCM authentication tags without explicit `authTagLength`
modules.name: dep0182:_short_gcm_authentication_tags_without_explicit_`authtaglength`

changes.description: Documentation-only deprecation.

modules.desc:
Type: Documentation-only (supports --pending-deprecation)

Applications that intend to use authentication tags that are shorter than the default authentication tag length should set the authTagLength option of the crypto.createDecipheriv() function to the appropriate length.

For ciphers in GCM mode, the decipher.setAuthTag() function accepts authentication tags of any valid length (see DEP0090). This behavior is deprecated to better align with recommendations per NIST SP 800-38D.
modules.displayName: DEP0182: Short GCM authentication tags without explicit `authTagLength`

modules.name: dep0183:_openssl_engine-based_apis

changes.description: Documentation-only deprecation.

modules.desc:
Type: Documentation-only

OpenSSL 3 has deprecated support for custom engines with a recommendation to switch to its new provider model. The clientCertEngine option for https.request(), tls.createSecureContext(), and tls.createServer(); the privateKeyEngine and privateKeyIdentifier for tls.createSecureContext(); and crypto.setEngine() all depend on this functionality from OpenSSL.

modules.name: dep0184:_instantiating_`node:zlib`_classes_without_`new`

changes.description: Documentation-only deprecation.

modules.desc:
Type: Documentation-only

Instantiating classes without the new qualifier exported by the node:zlib module is deprecated. It is recommended to use the new qualifier instead. This applies to all Zlib classes, such as Deflate, DeflateRaw, Gunzip, Inflate, InflateRaw, Unzip, and Zlib.

modules.name: dep0185:_instantiating_`node:repl`_classes_without_`new`

changes.description: Documentation-only deprecation.

modules.desc:
Type: Documentation-only

Instantiating classes without the new qualifier exported by the node:repl module is deprecated. It is recommended to use the new qualifier instead. This applies to all REPL classes, including REPLServer and Recoverable.

miscs.name: Errors
miscs.desc:
Applications running in Node.js will generally experience four categories of errors:

  • Standard JavaScript errors such as <EvalError>, <SyntaxError>, <RangeError>, <ReferenceError>, <TypeError>, and <URIError>.
  • System errors triggered by underlying operating system constraints such as attempting to open a file that does not exist or attempting to send data over a closed socket.
  • User-specified errors triggered by application code.
  • AssertionErrors are a special class of error that can be triggered when Node.js detects an exceptional logic violation that should never occur. These are raised typically by the node:assert module.

All JavaScript and system errors raised by Node.js inherit from, or are instances of, the standard JavaScript <Error> class and are guaranteed to provide at least the properties available on that class.

miscs.name: Error propagation and interception
miscs.desc:
Node.js supports several mechanisms for propagating and handling errors that occur while an application is running. How these errors are reported and handled depends entirely on the type of Error and the style of the API that is called.

All JavaScript errors are handled as exceptions that immediately generate and throw an error using the standard JavaScript throw mechanism. These are handled using the try…catch construct provided by the JavaScript language.

// Throws with a ReferenceError because z is not defined.
try {
  const m = 1;
  const n = m + z;
} catch (err) {
  // Handle the error here.
}

Any use of the JavaScript throw mechanism will raise an exception that must be handled or the Node.js process will exit immediately.

With few exceptions, Synchronous APIs (any blocking method that does not return a <Promise> nor accept a callback function, such as fs.readFileSync), will use throw to report errors.

Errors that occur within Asynchronous APIs may be reported in multiple ways:

  • Some asynchronous methods returns a <Promise>, you should always take into account that it might be rejected. See --unhandled-rejections flag for how the process will react to an unhandled promise rejection.

    const fs = require('fs/promises');

(async () => {
  let data;
  try {
    data = await fs.readFile('a file that does not exist');
  } catch (err) {
    console.error('There was an error reading the file!', err);
    return;
  }
  // Otherwise handle the data
})();

  • Most asynchronous methods that accept a callback function will accept an Error object passed as the first argument to that function. If that first argument is not null and is an instance of Error, then an error occurred that should be handled.

    const fs = require('node:fs');
fs.readFile('a file that does not exist', (err, data) => {
  if (err) {
    console.error('There was an error reading the file!', err);
    return;
  }
  // Otherwise handle the data
});

  • When an asynchronous method is called on an object that is an EventEmitter, errors can be routed to that object's 'error' event.

    const net = require('node:net');
const connection = net.connect('localhost');

// Adding an 'error' event handler to a stream:
connection.on('error', (err) => {
  // If the connection is reset by the server, or if it can't
  // connect at all, or on any sort of error encountered by
  // the connection, the error will be sent here.
  console.error(err);
});

connection.pipe(process.stdout);

  • A handful of typically asynchronous methods in the Node.js API may still use the throw mechanism to raise exceptions that must be handled using try…catch. There is no comprehensive list of such methods; please refer to the documentation of each method to determine the appropriate error handling mechanism required.

The use of the 'error' event mechanism is most common for stream-based and event emitter-based APIs, which themselves represent a series of asynchronous operations over time (as opposed to a single operation that may pass or fail).

For all EventEmitter objects, if an 'error' event handler is not provided, the error will be thrown, causing the Node.js process to report an uncaught exception and crash unless either: a handler has been registered for the 'uncaughtException' event, or the deprecated node:domain module is used.

const EventEmitter = require('node:events');
const ee = new EventEmitter();

setImmediate(() => {
  // This will crash the process because no 'error' event
  // handler has been added.
  ee.emit('error', new Error('This will crash'));
});

Errors generated in this way cannot be intercepted using try…catch as they are thrown after the calling code has already exited.

Developers must refer to the documentation for each method to determine exactly how errors raised by those methods are propagated.

miscs.name: Exceptions vs. errors
miscs.desc:
A JavaScript exception is a value that is thrown as a result of an invalid operation or as the target of a throw statement. While it is not required that these values are instances of Error or classes which inherit from Error, all exceptions thrown by Node.js or the JavaScript runtime will be instances of Error.

Some exceptions are unrecoverable at the JavaScript layer. Such exceptions will always cause the Node.js process to crash. Examples include assert() checks or abort() calls in the C++ layer.

Used when an operation has been aborted (typically using an AbortController).

APIs not using AbortSignals typically do not raise an error with this code.

This code does not use the regular ERR_* convention Node.js errors use in order to be compatible with the web platform's AbortError.

modules.desc: An operation was performed on a stream that had already been destroyed.

modules.name: `err_http2_max_pending_settings_ack`
modules.desc: Whenever an HTTP/2 SETTINGS frame is sent to a connected peer, the peer is required to send an acknowledgment that it has received and applied the new SETTINGS. By default, a maximum number of unacknowledged SETTINGS frames may be sent at any given time. This error code is used when that limit has been reached.

modules.name: `err_http2_nested_push`
modules.desc: An attempt was made to initiate a new push stream from within a push stream. Nested push streams are not permitted.

modules.name: `err_http2_no_mem`
modules.desc: Out of memory when using the http2session.setLocalWindowSize(windowSize) API.

modules.name: `err_http2_no_socket_manipulation`
modules.desc: An attempt was made to directly manipulate (read, write, pause, resume, etc.) a socket attached to an Http2Session.

modules.name: `err_http2_origin_length`
modules.desc: HTTP/2 ORIGIN frames are limited to a length of 16382 bytes.

modules.name: `err_http2_out_of_streams`
modules.desc: The number of streams created on a single HTTP/2 session reached the maximum limit.

modules.name: `err_http2_payload_forbidden`
modules.desc: A message payload was specified for an HTTP response code for which a payload is forbidden.

modules.name: `err_http2_ping_cancel`
modules.desc: An HTTP/2 ping was canceled.

modules.name: `err_http2_ping_length`
modules.desc: HTTP/2 ping payloads must be exactly 8 bytes in length.

modules.name: `err_http2_pseudoheader_not_allowed`
modules.desc: An HTTP/2 pseudo-header has been used inappropriately. Pseudo-headers are header key names that begin with the : prefix.

modules.name: `err_http2_push_disabled`
modules.desc: An attempt was made to create a push stream, which had been disabled by the client.

modules.name: `err_http2_send_file`
modules.desc: An attempt was made to use the Http2Stream.prototype.responseWithFile() API to send a directory.

modules.name: `err_http2_send_file_noseek`
modules.desc: An attempt was made to use the Http2Stream.prototype.responseWithFile() API to send something other than a regular file, but offset or length options were provided.

modules.name: `err_http2_session_error`
modules.desc: The Http2Session closed with a non-zero error code.

modules.name: `err_http2_settings_cancel`
modules.desc: The Http2Session settings canceled.

modules.name: `err_http2_socket_bound`
modules.desc: An attempt was made to connect a Http2Session object to a net.Socket or tls.TLSSocket that had already been bound to another Http2Session object.

modules.name: `err_http2_socket_unbound`
modules.desc: An attempt was made to use the socket property of an Http2Session that has already been closed.

modules.name: `err_http2_status_101`
modules.desc: Use of the 101 Informational status code is forbidden in HTTP/2.

modules.name: `err_http2_status_invalid`
modules.desc: An invalid HTTP status code has been specified. Status codes must be an integer between 100 and 599 (inclusive).

modules.name: `err_http2_stream_cancel`
modules.desc: An Http2Stream was destroyed before any data was transmitted to the connected peer.

modules.name: `err_http2_stream_error`
modules.desc: A non-zero error code was been specified in an RST_STREAM frame.

modules.name: `err_http2_stream_self_dependency`
modules.desc: When setting the priority for an HTTP/2 stream, the stream may be marked as a dependency for a parent stream. This error code is used when an attempt is made to mark a stream and dependent of itself.

modules.name: `err_http2_too_many_custom_settings`
modules.desc: The number of supported custom settings (10) has been exceeded.

modules.name: `err_http2_too_many_invalid_frames`
modules.desc: The limit of acceptable invalid HTTP/2 protocol frames sent by the peer, as specified through the maxSessionInvalidFrames option, has been exceeded.

modules.name: `err_http2_trailers_already_sent`
modules.desc: Trailing headers have already been sent on the Http2Stream.

modules.name: `err_http2_trailers_not_ready`
modules.desc: The http2stream.sendTrailers() method cannot be called until after the 'wantTrailers' event is emitted on an Http2Stream object. The 'wantTrailers' event will only be emitted if the waitForTrailers option is set for the Http2Stream.

modules.name: `err_http2_unsupported_protocol`
modules.desc: http2.connect() was passed a URL that uses any protocol other than http: or https:.

modules.name: `err_illegal_constructor`
modules.desc: An attempt was made to construct an object using a non-public constructor.

modules.name: `err_import_assertion_type_failed`
modules.desc: An import type attribute was provided, but the specified module is of a different type.

modules.name: `err_import_assertion_type_missing`
modules.desc: An import attribute is missing, preventing the specified module to be imported.

modules.name: `err_import_assertion_type_unsupported`
modules.desc: An import attribute is not supported by this version of Node.js.

modules.name: `err_import_attribute_unsupported`
modules.desc: An import attribute is not supported by this version of Node.js.

modules.name: `err_incompatible_option_pair`
modules.desc: An option pair is incompatible with each other and cannot be used at the same time.

modules.name: `err_input_type_not_allowed`
modules.desc: The --input-type flag was used to attempt to execute a file. This flag can only be used with input via --eval, --print, or STDIN.

modules.name: `err_inspector_already_activated`
modules.desc: While using the node:inspector module, an attempt was made to activate the inspector when it already started to listen on a port. Use inspector.close() before activating it on a different address.

modules.name: `err_inspector_already_connected`
modules.desc: While using the node:inspector module, an attempt was made to connect when the inspector was already connected.

modules.name: `err_inspector_closed`
modules.desc: While using the node:inspector module, an attempt was made to use the inspector after the session had already closed.

modules.name: `err_inspector_command`
modules.desc: An error occurred while issuing a command via the node:inspector module.

modules.name: `err_inspector_not_active`
modules.desc: The inspector is not active when inspector.waitForDebugger() is called.

modules.name: `err_inspector_not_available`
modules.desc: The node:inspector module is not available for use.

modules.name: `err_inspector_not_connected`
modules.desc: While using the node:inspector module, an attempt was made to use the inspector before it was connected.

modules.name: `err_inspector_not_worker`
modules.desc: An API was called on the main thread that can only be used from the worker thread.

modules.name: `err_internal_assertion`
modules.desc: There was a bug in Node.js or incorrect usage of Node.js internals. To fix the error, open an issue at https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues.

modules.name: `err_invalid_address`
modules.desc: The provided address is not understood by the Node.js API.

modules.name: `err_invalid_address_family`
modules.desc: The provided address family is not understood by the Node.js API.

modules.name: `err_invalid_arg_type`
modules.desc: An argument of the wrong type was passed to a Node.js API.

modules.name: `err_invalid_arg_value`
modules.desc: An invalid or unsupported value was passed for a given argument.

modules.name: `err_invalid_async_id`
modules.desc: An invalid asyncId or triggerAsyncId was passed using AsyncHooks. An id less than -1 should never happen.

modules.name: `err_invalid_buffer_size`
modules.desc: A swap was performed on a Buffer but its size was not compatible with the operation.

modules.name: `err_invalid_char`
modules.desc: Invalid characters were detected in headers.

modules.name: `err_invalid_cursor_pos`
modules.desc: A cursor on a given stream cannot be moved to a specified row without a specified column.

modules.name: `err_invalid_fd`
modules.desc: A file descriptor ('fd') was not valid (e.g. it was a negative value).

modules.name: `err_invalid_fd_type`
modules.desc: A file descriptor ('fd') type was not valid.

modules.name: `err_invalid_file_url_host`
modules.desc: A Node.js API that consumes file: URLs (such as certain functions in the fs module) encountered a file URL with an incompatible host. This situation can only occur on Unix-like systems where only localhost or an empty host is supported.

modules.name: `err_invalid_file_url_path`
modules.desc: A Node.js API that consumes file: URLs (such as certain functions in the fs module) encountered a file URL with an incompatible path. The exact semantics for determining whether a path can be used is platform-dependent.

modules.name: `err_invalid_handle_type`
modules.desc: An attempt was made to send an unsupported "handle" over an IPC communication channel to a child process. See subprocess.send() and process.send() for more information.

modules.name: `err_invalid_http_token`
modules.desc: An invalid HTTP token was supplied.

modules.name: `err_invalid_ip_address`
modules.desc: An IP address is not valid.

modules.name: `err_invalid_mime_syntax`
modules.desc: The syntax of a MIME is not valid.

modules.name: `err_invalid_module`
modules.desc: An attempt was made to load a module that does not exist or was otherwise not valid.

modules.name: `err_invalid_module_specifier`
modules.desc: The imported module string is an invalid URL, package name, or package subpath specifier.

modules.name: `err_invalid_object_define_property`
modules.desc: An error occurred while setting an invalid attribute on the property of an object.

modules.name: `err_invalid_package_config`
modules.desc: An invalid package.json file failed parsing.

modules.name: `err_invalid_package_target`
modules.desc: The package.json "exports" field contains an invalid target mapping value for the attempted module resolution.

modules.name: `err_invalid_performance_mark`
modules.desc: While using the Performance Timing API (perf_hooks), a performance mark is invalid.

modules.name: `err_invalid_protocol`
modules.desc: An invalid options.protocol was passed to http.request().

modules.name: `err_invalid_repl_eval_config`
modules.desc: Both breakEvalOnSigint and eval options were set in the REPL config, which is not supported.

modules.name: `err_invalid_repl_input`
modules.desc: The input may not be used in the REPL. The conditions under which this error is used are described in the REPL documentation.

modules.name: `err_invalid_return_property`
modules.desc: Thrown in case a function option does not provide a valid value for one of its returned object properties on execution.

modules.name: `err_invalid_return_property_value`
modules.desc: Thrown in case a function option does not provide an expected value type for one of its returned object properties on execution.

modules.name: `err_invalid_return_value`
modules.desc: Thrown in case a function option does not return an expected value type on execution, such as when a function is expected to return a promise.

modules.name: `err_invalid_state`
modules.desc: Indicates that an operation cannot be completed due to an invalid state. For instance, an object may have already been destroyed, or may be performing another operation.

modules.name: `err_invalid_sync_fork_input`
modules.desc: A Buffer, TypedArray, DataView, or string was provided as stdio input to an asynchronous fork. See the documentation for the child_process module for more information.

modules.name: `err_invalid_this`
modules.desc:
A Node.js API function was called with an incompatible this value.

const urlSearchParams = new URLSearchParams('foo=bar&baz=new');

const buf = Buffer.alloc(1);
urlSearchParams.has.call(buf, 'foo');
// Throws a TypeError with code 'ERR_INVALID_THIS'

modules.name: `err_invalid_transfer_object`
modules.desc: An invalid transfer object was passed to postMessage().

modules.name: `err_invalid_tuple`
modules.desc: An element in the iterable provided to the WHATWG URLSearchParams constructor did not represent a [name, value] tuple – that is, if an element is not iterable, or does not consist of exactly two elements.

modules.name: `err_invalid_uri`
modules.desc: An invalid URI was passed.

modules.name: `err_invalid_url`
modules.desc: An invalid URL was passed to the WHATWG URL constructor or the legacy url.parse() to be parsed. The thrown error object typically has an additional property 'input' that contains the URL that failed to parse.

modules.name: `err_invalid_url_scheme`
modules.desc: An attempt was made to use a URL of an incompatible scheme (protocol) for a specific purpose. It is only used in the WHATWG URL API support in the fs module (which only accepts URLs with 'file' scheme), but may be used in other Node.js APIs as well in the future.

modules.name: `err_ipc_channel_closed`
modules.desc: An attempt was made to use an IPC communication channel that was already closed.

modules.name: `err_ipc_disconnected`
modules.desc: An attempt was made to disconnect an IPC communication channel that was already disconnected. See the documentation for the child_process module for more information.

modules.name: `err_ipc_one_pipe`
modules.desc: An attempt was made to create a child Node.js process using more than one IPC communication channel. See the documentation for the child_process module for more information.

modules.name: `err_ipc_sync_fork`
modules.desc: An attempt was made to open an IPC communication channel with a synchronously forked Node.js process. See the documentation for the child_process module for more information.

modules.name: `err_loader_chain_incomplete`
modules.desc: An ESM loader hook returned without calling next() and without explicitly signaling a short circuit.

modules.name: `err_manifest_assert_integrity`
modules.desc: An attempt was made to load a resource, but the resource did not match the integrity defined by the policy manifest. See the documentation for policy manifests for more information.

modules.name: `err_manifest_dependency_missing`
modules.desc: An attempt was made to load a resource, but the resource was not listed as a dependency from the location that attempted to load it. See the documentation for policy manifests for more information.

modules.name: `err_manifest_integrity_mismatch`
modules.desc: An attempt was made to load a policy manifest, but the manifest had multiple entries for a resource which did not match each other. Update the manifest entries to match in order to resolve this error. See the documentation for policy manifests for more information.

modules.name: `err_manifest_invalid_resource_field`
modules.desc: A policy manifest resource had an invalid value for one of its fields. Update the manifest entry to match in order to resolve this error. See the documentation for policy manifests for more information.

modules.name: `err_manifest_invalid_specifier`
modules.desc: A policy manifest resource had an invalid value for one of its dependency mappings. Update the manifest entry to match to resolve this error. See the documentation for policy manifests for more information.

modules.name: `err_manifest_parse_policy`
modules.desc: An attempt was made to load a policy manifest, but the manifest was unable to be parsed. See the documentation for policy manifests for more information.

modules.name: `err_manifest_tdz`
modules.desc: An attempt was made to read from a policy manifest, but the manifest initialization has not yet taken place. This is likely a bug in Node.js.

modules.name: `err_manifest_unknown_onerror`
modules.desc: A policy manifest was loaded, but had an unknown value for its "onerror" behavior. See the documentation for policy manifests for more information.

modules.name: `err_memory_allocation_failed`
modules.desc: An attempt was made to allocate memory (usually in the C++ layer) but it failed.

modules.name: `err_message_target_context_unavailable`
modules.desc: A message posted to a MessagePort could not be deserialized in the target vm Context. Not all Node.js objects can be successfully instantiated in any context at this time, and attempting to transfer them using postMessage() can fail on the receiving side in that case.

modules.name: `err_method_not_implemented`
modules.desc: A method is required but not implemented.

modules.name: `err_missing_args`
modules.desc: A required argument of a Node.js API was not passed. This is only used for strict compliance with the API specification (which in some cases may accept func(undefined) but not func()). In most native Node.js APIs, func(undefined) and func() are treated identically, and the ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE error code may be used instead.

modules.name: `err_missing_option`
modules.desc: For APIs that accept options objects, some options might be mandatory. This code is thrown if a required option is missing.

modules.name: `err_missing_passphrase`
modules.desc: An attempt was made to read an encrypted key without specifying a passphrase.

modules.name: `err_missing_platform_for_worker`
modules.desc: The V8 platform used by this instance of Node.js does not support creating Workers. This is caused by lack of embedder support for Workers. In particular, this error will not occur with standard builds of Node.js.

modules.name: `err_missing_transferable_in_transfer_list`
modules.desc:
An object that needs to be explicitly listed in the transferList argument is in the object passed to a postMessage() call, but is not provided in the transferList for that call. Usually, this is a MessagePort.

In Node.js versions prior to v15.0.0, the error code being used here was ERR_MISSING_MESSAGE_PORT_IN_TRANSFER_LIST. However, the set of transferable object types has been expanded to cover more types than MessagePort.

modules.name: `err_module_not_found`
modules.desc: A module file could not be resolved by the ECMAScript modules loader while attempting an import operation or when loading the program entry point.

modules.name: `err_multiple_callback`
modules.desc:
A callback was called more than once.

A callback is almost always meant to only be called once as the query can either be fulfilled or rejected but not both at the same time. The latter would be possible by calling a callback more than once.

modules.name: `err_napi_cons_function`
modules.desc: While using Node-API, a constructor passed was not a function.

modules.name: `err_napi_invalid_dataview_args`
modules.desc: While calling napi_create_dataview(), a given offset was outside the bounds of the dataview or offset + length was larger than a length of given buffer.

modules.name: `err_napi_invalid_typedarray_alignment`
modules.desc: While calling napi_create_typedarray(), the provided offset was not a multiple of the element size.

modules.name: `err_napi_invalid_typedarray_length`
modules.desc: While calling napi_create_typedarray(), (length * size_of_element) + byte_offset was larger than the length of given buffer.

modules.name: `err_napi_tsfn_call_js`
modules.desc: An error occurred while invoking the JavaScript portion of the thread-safe function.

modules.name: `err_napi_tsfn_get_undefined`
modules.desc: An error occurred while attempting to retrieve the JavaScript undefined value.

modules.name: `err_napi_tsfn_start_idle_loop`
modules.desc: On the main thread, values are removed from the queue associated with the thread-safe function in an idle loop. This error indicates that an error has occurred when attempting to start the loop.

modules.name: `err_napi_tsfn_stop_idle_loop`
modules.desc: Once no more items are left in the queue, the idle loop must be suspended. This error indicates that the idle loop has failed to stop.

modules.name: `err_not_building_snapshot`
modules.desc: An attempt was made to use operations that can only be used when building V8 startup snapshot even though Node.js isn't building one.

modules.name: `err_not_in_single_executable_application`
modules.desc: The operation cannot be performed when it's not in a single-executable application.

modules.name: `err_not_supported_in_snapshot`
modules.desc: An attempt was made to perform operations that are not supported when building a startup snapshot.

modules.name: `err_no_crypto`
modules.desc: An attempt was made to use crypto features while Node.js was not compiled with OpenSSL crypto support.

modules.name: `err_no_icu`
modules.desc: An attempt was made to use features that require ICU, but Node.js was not compiled with ICU support.

modules.name: `err_non_context_aware_disabled`
modules.desc: A non-context-aware native addon was loaded in a process that disallows them.

modules.name: `err_out_of_range`
modules.desc: A given value is out of the accepted range.

modules.name: `err_package_import_not_defined`
modules.desc: The package.json "imports" field does not define the given internal package specifier mapping.

modules.name: `err_package_path_not_exported`
modules.desc: The package.json "exports" field does not export the requested subpath. Because exports are encapsulated, private internal modules that are not exported cannot be imported through the package resolution, unless using an absolute URL.

modules.name: `err_parse_args_invalid_option_value`
modules.desc: When strict set to true, thrown by util.parseArgs() if a <boolean> value is provided for an option of type <string>, or if a <string> value is provided for an option of type <boolean>.

modules.name: `err_parse_args_unexpected_positional`
modules.desc: Thrown by util.parseArgs(), when a positional argument is provided and allowPositionals is set to false.

modules.name: `err_parse_args_unknown_option`
modules.desc: When strict set to true, thrown by util.parseArgs() if an argument is not configured in options.

modules.name: `err_performance_invalid_timestamp`
modules.desc: An invalid timestamp value was provided for a performance mark or measure.

modules.name: `err_performance_measure_invalid_options`
modules.desc: Invalid options were provided for a performance measure.

modules.name: `err_proto_access`
modules.desc: Accessing Object.prototype.__proto__ has been forbidden using --disable-proto=throw. Object.getPrototypeOf and Object.setPrototypeOf should be used to get and set the prototype of an object.

modules.name: `err_require_cycle_module`
modules.desc:
When trying to require() a ES Module, a CommonJS to ESM or ESM to CommonJS edge participates in an immediate cycle. This is not allowed because ES Modules cannot be evaluated while they are already being evaluated.

To avoid the cycle, the require() call involved in a cycle should not happen at the top-level of either an ES Module (via createRequire()) or a CommonJS module, and should be done lazily in an inner function.

modules.name: `err_require_async_module`
modules.desc:
When trying to require() a ES Module, the module turns out to be asynchronous. That is, it contains top-level await.

To see where the top-level await is, use --experimental-print-required-tla (this would execute the modules before looking for the top-level awaits).

modules.name: `err_require_esm`

changes.description: require() now supports loading synchronous ES modules by default.

modules.desc:
An attempt was made to require() an ES Module.

This error has been deprecated since require() now supports loading synchronous ES modules. When require() encounters an ES module that contains top-level await, it will throw ERR_REQUIRE_ASYNC_MODULE instead.

modules.name: `err_script_execution_interrupted`
modules.desc: Script execution was interrupted by SIGINT (For example, Ctrl+C was pressed.)

modules.name: `err_script_execution_timeout`
modules.desc: Script execution timed out, possibly due to bugs in the script being executed.

modules.name: `err_server_already_listen`
modules.desc: The server.listen() method was called while a net.Server was already listening. This applies to all instances of net.Server, including HTTP, HTTPS, and HTTP/2 Server instances.

modules.name: `err_server_not_running`
modules.desc: The server.close() method was called when a net.Server was not running. This applies to all instances of net.Server, including HTTP, HTTPS, and HTTP/2 Server instances.

modules.name: `err_single_executable_application_asset_not_found`
modules.desc: A key was passed to single executable application APIs to identify an asset, but no match could be found.

modules.name: `err_socket_already_bound`
modules.desc: An attempt was made to bind a socket that has already been bound.

modules.name: `err_socket_bad_buffer_size`
modules.desc: An invalid (negative) size was passed for either the recvBufferSize or sendBufferSize options in dgram.createSocket().

modules.name: `err_socket_bad_port`
modules.desc: An API function expecting a port >= 0 and < 65536 received an invalid value.

modules.name: `err_socket_bad_type`
modules.desc: An API function expecting a socket type (udp4 or udp6) received an invalid value.

modules.name: `err_socket_buffer_size`
modules.desc: While using dgram.createSocket(), the size of the receive or send Buffer could not be determined.

modules.name: `err_socket_closed`
modules.desc: An attempt was made to operate on an already closed socket.

modules.name: `err_socket_closed_before_connection`
modules.desc: When calling net.Socket.write() on a connecting socket and the socket was closed before the connection was established.

modules.name: `err_socket_connection_timeout`
modules.desc: The socket was unable to connect to any address returned by the DNS within the allowed timeout when using the family autoselection algorithm.

modules.name: `err_socket_dgram_is_connected`
modules.desc: A dgram.connect() call was made on an already connected socket.

modules.name: `err_socket_dgram_not_connected`
modules.desc: A dgram.disconnect() or dgram.remoteAddress() call was made on a disconnected socket.

modules.name: `err_socket_dgram_not_running`
modules.desc: A call was made and the UDP subsystem was not running.

modules.name: `err_sri_parse`
modules.desc: A string was provided for a Subresource Integrity check, but was unable to be parsed. Check the format of integrity attributes by looking at the Subresource Integrity specification.

modules.name: `err_stream_already_finished`
modules.desc: A stream method was called that cannot complete because the stream was finished.

modules.name: `err_stream_cannot_pipe`
modules.desc: An attempt was made to call stream.pipe() on a Writable stream.

modules.name: `err_stream_destroyed`
modules.desc: A stream method was called that cannot complete because the stream was destroyed using stream.destroy().

modules.name: `err_stream_null_values`
modules.desc: An attempt was made to call stream.write() with a null chunk.

modules.name: `err_stream_premature_close`
modules.desc: An error returned by stream.finished() and stream.pipeline(), when a stream or a pipeline ends non gracefully with no explicit error.

modules.name: `err_stream_push_after_eof`
modules.desc: An attempt was made to call stream.push() after a null(EOF) had been pushed to the stream.

modules.name: `err_stream_unshift_after_end_event`
modules.desc: An attempt was made to call stream.unshift() after the 'end' event was emitted.

modules.name: `err_stream_wrap`
modules.desc:
Prevents an abort if a string decoder was set on the Socket or if the decoder is in objectMode.

const Socket = require('node:net').Socket;
const instance = new Socket();

instance.setEncoding('utf8');

modules.name: `err_stream_write_after_end`
modules.desc: An attempt was made to call stream.write() after stream.end() has been called.

modules.name: `err_string_too_long`
modules.desc: An attempt has been made to create a string longer than the maximum allowed length.

modules.name: `err_synthetic`
modules.desc: An artificial error object used to capture the call stack for diagnostic reports.

modules.name: `err_system_error`
modules.desc: An unspecified or non-specific system error has occurred within the Node.js process. The error object will have an err.info object property with additional details.

modules.name: `err_test_failure`
modules.desc: This error represents a failed test. Additional information about the failure is available via the cause property. The failureType property specifies what the test was doing when the failure occurred.

modules.name: `err_tls_alpn_callback_invalid_result`
modules.desc: This error is thrown when an ALPNCallback returns a value that is not in the list of ALPN protocols offered by the client.

modules.name: `err_tls_alpn_callback_with_protocols`
modules.desc: This error is thrown when creating a TLSServer if the TLS options include both ALPNProtocols and ALPNCallback. These options are mutually exclusive.

modules.name: `err_tls_cert_altname_format`
modules.desc: This error is thrown by checkServerIdentity if a user-supplied subjectaltname property violates encoding rules. Certificate objects produced by Node.js itself always comply with encoding rules and will never cause this error.

modules.name: `err_tls_cert_altname_invalid`
modules.desc: While using TLS, the host name/IP of the peer did not match any of the subjectAltNames in its certificate.

modules.name: `err_tls_dh_param_size`
modules.desc: While using TLS, the parameter offered for the Diffie-Hellman (DH) key-agreement protocol is too small. By default, the key length must be greater than or equal to 1024 bits to avoid vulnerabilities, even though it is strongly recommended to use 2048 bits or larger for stronger security.

modules.name: `err_tls_handshake_timeout`
modules.desc: A TLS/SSL handshake timed out. In this case, the server must also abort the connection.

modules.name: `err_tls_invalid_context`
modules.desc: The context must be a SecureContext.

modules.name: `err_tls_invalid_protocol_method`
modules.desc: The specified secureProtocol method is invalid. It is either unknown, or disabled because it is insecure.

classes.name: Error
classes.desc:
A generic JavaScript <Error> object that does not denote any specific circumstance of why the error occurred. Error objects capture a "stack trace" detailing the point in the code at which the Error was instantiated, and may provide a text description of the error.

All errors generated by Node.js, including all system and JavaScript errors, will either be instances of, or inherit from, the Error class.

methods.name: captureStackTrace
methods.desc:
Creates a .stack property on targetObject, which when accessed returns a string representing the location in the code at which Error.captureStackTrace() was called.

const myObject = {};
Error.captureStackTrace(myObject);
myObject.stack;  // Similar to `new Error().stack`

The first line of the trace will be prefixed with ${myObject.name}: ${myObject.message}.

The optional constructorOpt argument accepts a function. If given, all frames above constructorOpt, including constructorOpt, will be omitted from the generated stack trace.

The constructorOpt argument is useful for hiding implementation details of error generation from the user. For instance:

function a() {
  b();
}

function b() {
  c();
}

function c() {
  // Create an error without stack trace to avoid calculating the stack trace twice.
  const { stackTraceLimit } = Error;
  Error.stackTraceLimit = 0;
  const error = new Error();
  Error.stackTraceLimit = stackTraceLimit;

  // Capture the stack trace above function b
  Error.captureStackTrace(error, b); // Neither function c, nor b is included in the stack trace
  throw error;
}

a();

properties.name: stackTraceLimit
properties.desc:
The Error.stackTraceLimit property specifies the number of stack frames collected by a stack trace (whether generated by new Error().stack or Error.captureStackTrace(obj)).

The default value is 10 but may be set to any valid JavaScript number. Changes will affect any stack trace captured after the value has been changed.

If set to a non-number value, or set to a negative number, stack traces will not capture any frames.

properties.name: cause
properties.desc:
If present, the error.cause property is the underlying cause of the Error. It is used when catching an error and throwing a new one with a different message or code in order to still have access to the original error.

The error.cause property is typically set by calling new Error(message, { cause }). It is not set by the constructor if the cause option is not provided.

This property allows errors to be chained. When serializing Error objects, util.inspect() recursively serializes error.cause if it is set.

const cause = new Error('The remote HTTP server responded with a 500 status');
const symptom = new Error('The message failed to send', { cause });

console.log(symptom);
// Prints:
//   Error: The message failed to send
//       at REPL2:1:17
//       at Script.runInThisContext (node:vm:130:12)
//       ... 7 lines matching cause stack trace ...
//       at [_line] [as _line] (node:internal/readline/interface:886:18) {
//     [cause]: Error: The remote HTTP server responded with a 500 status
//         at REPL1:1:15
//         at Script.runInThisContext (node:vm:130:12)
//         at REPLServer.defaultEval (node:repl:574:29)
//         at bound (node:domain:426:15)
//         at REPLServer.runBound [as eval] (node:domain:437:12)
//         at REPLServer.onLine (node:repl:902:10)
//         at REPLServer.emit (node:events:549:35)
//         at REPLServer.emit (node:domain:482:12)
//         at [_onLine] [as _onLine] (node:internal/readline/interface:425:12)
//         at [_line] [as _line] (node:internal/readline/interface:886:18)

properties.name: code
properties.desc: The error.code property is a string label that identifies the kind of error. error.code is the most stable way to identify an error. It will only change between major versions of Node.js. In contrast, error.message strings may change between any versions of Node.js. See Node.js error codes for details about specific codes.

properties.name: message
properties.desc:
The error.message property is the string description of the error as set by calling new Error(message). The message passed to the constructor will also appear in the first line of the stack trace of the Error, however changing this property after the Error object is created may not change the first line of the stack trace (for example, when error.stack is read before this property is changed).

const err = new Error('The message');
console.error(err.message);
// Prints: The message

properties.name: stack
properties.desc:
The error.stack property is a string describing the point in the code at which the Error was instantiated.

Error: Things keep happening!
   at /home/gbusey/file.js:525:2
   at Frobnicator.refrobulate (/home/gbusey/business-logic.js:424:21)
   at Actor.<anonymous> (/home/gbusey/actors.js:400:8)
   at increaseSynergy (/home/gbusey/actors.js:701:6)

The first line is formatted as <error class name>: <error message>, and is followed by a series of stack frames (each line beginning with "at "). Each frame describes a call site within the code that lead to the error being generated. V8 attempts to display a name for each function (by variable name, function name, or object method name), but occasionally it will not be able to find a suitable name. If V8 cannot determine a name for the function, only location information will be displayed for that frame. Otherwise, the determined function name will be displayed with location information appended in parentheses.

Frames are only generated for JavaScript functions. If, for example, execution synchronously passes through a C++ addon function called cheetahify which itself calls a JavaScript function, the frame representing the cheetahify call will not be present in the stack traces:

const cheetahify = require('./native-binding.node');

function makeFaster() {
  // `cheetahify()` *synchronously* calls speedy.
  cheetahify(function speedy() {
    throw new Error('oh no!');
  });
}

makeFaster();
// will throw:
//   /home/gbusey/file.js:6
//       throw new Error('oh no!');
//           ^
//   Error: oh no!
//       at speedy (/home/gbusey/file.js:6:11)
//       at makeFaster (/home/gbusey/file.js:5:3)
//       at Object.<anonymous> (/home/gbusey/file.js:10:1)
//       at Module._compile (module.js:456:26)
//       at Object.Module._extensions..js (module.js:474:10)
//       at Module.load (module.js:356:32)
//       at Function.Module._load (module.js:312:12)
//       at Function.Module.runMain (module.js:497:10)
//       at startup (node.js:119:16)
//       at node.js:906:3

The location information will be one of:

  • native, if the frame represents a call internal to V8 (as in [].forEach).
  • plain-filename.js:line:column, if the frame represents a call internal to Node.js.
  • /absolute/path/to/file.js:line:column, if the frame represents a call in a user program (using CommonJS module system), or its dependencies.
  • <transport-protocol>:///url/to/module/file.mjs:line:column, if the frame represents a call in a user program (using ES module system), or its dependencies.

The string representing the stack trace is lazily generated when the error.stack property is accessed.

The number of frames captured by the stack trace is bounded by the smaller of Error.stackTraceLimit or the number of available frames on the current event loop tick.

options.textRaw: `cause` {any} The error that caused the newly created error.
options.name: cause
options.desc: The error that caused the newly created error.

signatures.desc: Creates a new Error object and sets the error.message property to the provided text message. If an object is passed as message, the text message is generated by calling String(message). If the cause option is provided, it is assigned to the error.cause property. The error.stack property will represent the point in the code at which new Error() was called. Stack traces are dependent on V8's stack trace API. Stack traces extend only to either (a) the beginning of synchronous code execution, or (b) the number of frames given by the property Error.stackTraceLimit, whichever is smaller.

classes.name: AssertionError
classes.desc:
• Extends: <errors.Error>

Indicates the failure of an assertion. For details, see Class: assert.AssertionError.

classes.name: RangeError
classes.desc:
• Extends: <errors.Error>

Indicates that a provided argument was not within the set or range of acceptable values for a function; whether that is a numeric range, or outside the set of options for a given function parameter.

require('node:net').connect(-1);
// Throws "RangeError: "port" option should be >= 0 and < 65536: -1"

Node.js will generate and throw RangeError instances immediately as a form of argument validation.

classes.name: ReferenceError
classes.desc:
• Extends: <errors.Error>

Indicates that an attempt is being made to access a variable that is not defined. Such errors commonly indicate typos in code, or an otherwise broken program.

While client code may generate and propagate these errors, in practice, only V8 will do so.

doesNotExist;
// Throws ReferenceError, doesNotExist is not a variable in this program.

Unless an application is dynamically generating and running code, ReferenceError instances indicate a bug in the code or its dependencies.

classes.name: SyntaxError
classes.desc:
• Extends: <errors.Error>

Indicates that a program is not valid JavaScript. These errors may only be generated and propagated as a result of code evaluation. Code evaluation may happen as a result of eval, Function, require, or vm. These errors are almost always indicative of a broken program.

try {
  require('node:vm').runInThisContext('binary ! isNotOk');
} catch (err) {
  // 'err' will be a SyntaxError.
}

SyntaxError instances are unrecoverable in the context that created them – they may only be caught by other contexts.

classes.name: SystemError
classes.desc:
• Extends: <errors.Error>

Node.js generates system errors when exceptions occur within its runtime environment. These usually occur when an application violates an operating system constraint. For example, a system error will occur if an application attempts to read a file that does not exist.

  • address <string> If present, the address to which a network connection failed
  • code <string> The string error code
  • dest <string> If present, the file path destination when reporting a file system error
  • errno <number> The system-provided error number
  • info <Object> If present, extra details about the error condition
  • message <string> A system-provided human-readable description of the error
  • path <string> If present, the file path when reporting a file system error
  • port <number> If present, the network connection port that is not available
  • syscall <string> The name of the system call that triggered the error

On Windows the error number provided by the system will be normalized by libuv.

To get the string representation of the error code, use util.getSystemErrorName(error.errno).
